# Chapter 2 — sketch answers {.unnumbered}

\(1\) You cannot protect what you do not understand. Failure modes: Protecting
the wrong things because the critical assets were never identified, and being
blindsided when an unknown dependency (a supplier, a single system) fails --- in
both cases effort is spent in the wrong places at real cost. (2) Any sound
answer works; the pattern is: The model names what the organisation depends on
(resources, channels, revenue), the chain shows which activity carries the most
value, and the process pins possible harm to specific steps. (3) Value
concentrates at the checkout, where it is captured; a denial-of-service there
stops revenue, which is risk R2. The vault analogy is apt because protection
should follow value, not be spread evenly --- the jeweller guards the vault, not
the stationery cupboard. (4) Because the auditor cannot judge where the risks of
the engagement lie without knowing the business and its environment; risk
assessment in this course rests on the same discipline --- understanding the
entity first is what makes the later judgements trustworthy in both professions.
(5) Key resource: The customer database (R3). Channel: The webshop, whose login
step carries account takeover (R1). Revenue stream: Sales through the checkout,
interrupted by denial-of-service (R2).
